caveat: These are test-environment measurements on a small dataset. They are a STRUCTURAL baseline (query counts are the meaningful signal) and must NOT be presented as production latency SLOs. Production benchmarking requires a production-representative dataset and hardware.

findings.assessment: GOOD - eager loading is effective; no N+1 in this path.

findings.observation: booking_list allocates ~1.17 MB for 50 eager-loaded bookings with screens
findings.assessment: WATCH - acceptable at this size; worth re-measuring against production row counts and average screens-per-booking.

findings.observation: All other probed read paths issue exactly 1 query
73 N+1 candidates were flagged by a lexical heuristic
findings.assessment: NOT CONFIRMED. The measured eager-loaded paths above show no N+1. The heuristic is proximity-based and produces false positives; it is recorded as a candidate list only and was not used to justify any change.

unmeasured: BookingCapacityService::checkAvailability could not be measured - the probe used the wrong method signature. Requires a correctly-shaped fixture.
HTTP-level latency (including middleware, serialisation and auth) was not measured.
No load or concurrency testing was performed.
changes_made: None. No index, cache, eager-load or pagination change was made, because no measured regression justified a behaviour-affecting optimisation.
